analyst.summary: Cummins India had a genuinely strong FY26 - revenue up 17%, profit up 18%, powered mainly by data-centre-linked power-generation demand and CPCB IV+ emission-norm-compliant products, with the aftermarket/service business also compounding nicely as older engines start coming off warranty. It is a very high-quality, debt-free company with excellent returns on capital. The concern is entirely about price: at roughly 62-66 times trailing earnings, the stock already reflects many years of continued high growth from data centres alone, even though management itself only guides 3-4 years of visibility on that demand and two other parts of the business (industrial equipment and exports) are currently flat to declining. With a well-funded competitor (Kirloskar) now entering the same high-horsepower data-centre segment, we would not add fresh money at this valuation and rate it a Sell on stretched pricing, not on any deterioration in the underlying business.
